trial_name.text: CL-0600-020 (Study 020), the pivotal adequate and well-controlled study

citations.quote: The efficacy of the 0.05 mg/kg/day teduglutide dose, for which the applicant is pursuing labeling, was principally demonstrated in trial CL-0600-020.

a Phase 3, multicenter, randomized, double-blind, parallel-group placebo-controlled study (CL0600-020) which serves as the lone adequate and well controlled study of this clinical development program as per 21 CFR 314.126

design.text: 24-week multicenter, double-blind, randomized, parallel-group, placebo-controlled trial; subjects randomized 1:1 to placebo or teduglutide 0.05 mg/kg/day

citations.quote: CL-0600-020 was a 24-week multicenter, double-blind, randomized, parallel group, placebo-controlled
subjects were randomized in a 1:1 ratio to placebo or teduglutide 0.05 mg/kg/day

population.text: Adult patients with Short Bowel Syndrome who are dependent on parenteral nutrition/IV fluids

citations.quote: a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group, multi-national, multi-center, clinical trial (CL0600-020) in adults with SBS

endpoint.text: Binary Response: number and percentage of subjects achieving at least a 20% reduction from baseline in weekly PN volume at Week 20 sustained through Week 24

citations.quote: **Primary Endpoint:** Binary Response i.e. the number and percentage of subjects who demonstrated a response at Week 20, and who sustained that response through Week 24. Response was defined as the achievement of at least a 20% reduction from Baseline in weekly PN volume.
There were 86 ITT subjects (43 teduglutide and 43 placebo).

Study 020 demonstrated a statistically significant (p=0.002) difference between teduglutide and placebo for the primary endpoint (percent responders in each study group who achieved at least 20% reduction in weekly PN/I.V. volume at Weeks 20 and 24): 62.8% versus 30.2% (teduglutide versus placebo).

indication.text: Treatment of adult patients with Short Bowel Syndrome (SBS) who are dependent on parenteral support

citations.quote: GATTEX® (teduglutide [rDNA origin]) for injection is a glucagon-like peptide-2 (GLP-2) analog indicated for the treatment of adult patients with Short Bowel Syndrome (SBS) who are dependent on parenteral support. (1)

target_moa.text: A recombinant analog of human glucagon-like peptide-2 (GLP-2); a GLP-2 receptor agonist that promotes growth and repair of intestinal epithelium (increased villus height and crypt depth), improving intestinal absorption

citations.quote: GATTEX (teduglutide) is a human recombinant analog (E. Coli) of glucagon-like peptide-2 (GLP-2).
GLP-2 is believed to promote growth and repair of intestinal epithelium.
Teduglutide has been shown to increase villus height and crypt depth of the intestinal epithelium resulting in enhanced absorptive capacity of the intestine.

Teduglutide is a 33 amino acid peptide that differs from its natural analog, glucagon-like peptide-2 (GLP-2) receptor agonist in the substitution of alanine (in native GLP-2) for glycine at the second position at the N-terminus.

key_safety.text: Most common adverse reactions (>=10%) across all studies (n=566): abdominal pain (30.0%), injection site reactions (22.4%), nausea (18.2%), headaches (15.9%), abdominal distension (13.8%), upper respiratory tract infection (11.8%). Serious risks based on mechanism of action include possible acceleration of neoplastic growth and enhanced colorectal polyp growth, intestinal obstruction, and biliary and pancreatic disease.

citations.quote: The most commonly reported (\ge 10\%) adverse reactions in patients treated with GATTEX across all clinical studies (n = 566) were: abdominal pain (30.0%); injection site reactions (22.4%); nausea (18.2%); headaches (15.9%); abdominal distension (13.8%); upper respiratory tract infection (11.8%).

Adverse events which occurred less frequently and were related to the mechanism of action of Gattex include possible acceleration of neoplastic growth and enhancement of colon polyp growth, gastrointestinal obstruction, and biliary and pancreatic disorders.

detail.text: A REMS is required consisting of a communication plan and elements to assure safe use to mitigate the risk of possible acceleration of neoplastic growth and enhancement of colon polyp growth, gastrointestinal obstruction, and biliary and pancreatic disorders.

citations.quote: In accordance with section 505-1 of FDCA, we have determined that a REMS is necessary for GATTEX (teduglutide [rDNA origin]) to ensure the benefits of the drug outweigh the risks of possible acceleration of neoplastic growth and enhancement of colon polyp growth, gastrointestinal obstruction, and biliary and pancreatic disorders associated with GATTEX (teduglutide [rDNA origin]).
The REMS consists of a communication plan, elements to assure safe use, and a timetable for submission of assessments of the REMS.

vote.text: Gastrointestinal Drugs Advisory Committee (GIDAC) met October 16, 2012; voted unanimously 12 YES, 0 NO that a clinically meaningful benefit was demonstrated in adult SBS patients.

citations.quote: The Gastrointestinal Drugs AC Committee (GIDAC) met on October 16, 2012.
**Discussion:** Unanimous agreement. 12 YES, 0 NO.

requirement.text: 1978-1: A prospective, multi-center, long-term observational registry study of SBS patients treated with teduglutide to assess long-term safety and rule out a clinically meaningful increase in colorectal cancer risk; patients enrolled over 5 years and followed at least 10 years.

citations.quote: 1978-1 A prospective, multi-center, long-term, observational, registry study, of short bowel syndrome patients treated with teduglutide in a routine clinical setting, to assess the long-term safety of teduglutide. Design the study around a testable hypothesis to rule out a clinically meaningful increase in colorectal cancer risk above an estimated background risk in a suitable comparator.
Patients should be enrolled over an initial 5-year period and then followed for a period of at least 10 years from the time of enrollment.

requirement.text: 1978-2: Elemental impurities specifications will be expanded to include limits and testing for all metals, as recommended in USP <232>.

description.text: Expanded indication to include pediatric patients 1 year of age and older with Short Bowel Syndrome who are dependent on parenteral support

citations.quote: This Prior Approval sNDA provides for the expansion of the indication to pediatric patients 1 year of age and older with Short Bowel Syndrome (SBS) who are dependent on parenteral support, and proposes modifications to the approved GATTEX (teduglutide) Risk Evaluation and Mitigation Strategy (REMS).
